messages:
sanjay: Heads up — we're seeing 1-3% packet loss on the overlay between gpu-node-a and gpu-node-b in us-west-2 during sustained large-batch inference. Errors spike around 1m-3m windows during model hot-paths.

mike: Noted. Which CNI are those nodes on? geneve or vxlan?

sanjay: Cilium in geneve mode (MTU 1450 configured cluster-wide), but host NICs are 9000 (jumbo) on our GPU boxes.

anya: Do you have tcpdump/iperf from pod->pod and node->node? Could be offload/segmentation mismatch.

sanjay: I ran quick iperf3 from pod on node-a -> pod on node-b for 120s: 
```
# iperf3 -c 10.0.4.12 -t 120
[ ID]   Interval          Transfer     Bandwidth
[SUM]  0.00-120.00 sec  20.1 GBytes  1.44 Gbits/sec
[SUM]  Retr  3400/1250000 (0.27%)
```
Loss shows up as retransmissions.

mike: 0.27% retrans isn't huge but for real-time GPU work it's bad. Check geneve device offloads: 
```sh
# ethtool -k genev_sys_12345
Features for genev_sys_12345:
 rx-checksumming: off
 tx-checksumming: off
 scatter-gather: on
 tcp-segmentation-offload: on
 generic-segmentation-offload: on
 generic-receive-offload: on
```
If host NIC is doing TSO/GSO and overlay expects different pkt sizes that can cause packet coalescing and reordering.

anya: Also verify kernel dmesg for NETDEV alerts, and host NIC IRQ balancing. I saw one dmesg spam earlier: 
```
[ 1234.567890] geneve: skb->len 1500 > max frame size 1496, dropping
```
That suggests MTU mismatch somewhere.

sanjay: I checked: ip link show on host says eno1 mtu 9000, cilium_vxlan mtu 1450, but geneve device shows mtu 1500 on the node for some reason.

infra-bot: PacketLossAlert: {"src_node":"gpu-node-a","dst_node":"gpu-node-b","loss_pct":"1.2","alert_ts":"1732501200"}

mike: There's your problem — geneve device MTU mismatch. Cilium expects 1450 but kernel created geneve with 1500. Either Cilium init didn't apply or something changed. Quick fix: 
```sh
sudo ip link set dev genev_sys_12345 mtu 1450
# verify
ip link show genev_sys_12345
```
After that, re-run iperf.

sanjay: Doing it now on both nodes. Applying on gpu-node-a and gpu-node-b...

sanjay: Re-ran iperf3 120s: 
```
[SUM]  Retr  20/1250000 (0.0016%)
```
Looks much better.

anya: Nice. Followups: 1) add a node-level check to ensure overlay devices inherit CNI MTU on boot; 2) audit our init scripts — why did geneve get created with 1500 when cilium config is 1450? Could be kernel/geneve module default.

mike: Agreed. Also check GRO/TSO on the host for geneve and physical NICs. For high throughput, disabling generic-receive-offload on the overlay sometimes reduces reordering issues: 
```sh
ethtool -K genev_sys_12345 gro off gso off tso off
```
But only do that if CPU overhead is acceptable.

sanjay: I'll add a one-off daemonset to enforce mtu + offload settings and create a bug for Cilium init ordering.

anya: One more thought — if we hit places where RDMA is used between GPUs (intra-node), overlay shouldn't affect it, but ensure our placement avoids cross-host RDMA over geneve.

mike: Filed infra ticket INFRA-7823 to add the daemonset and a cluster-check at boot (MTU and offloads).

sanjay: Thanks. Keeping an eye on the nodes for the next 24h and will rollback daemonset if CPU climbs. :thumbsup:
